name: canli-mcp

tools.name: find_tool
tools.description: Search the 401 finance tools (packs: quant, validation, fundamentals, research, backtest, markets) in plain words, e.g. "deflated sharpe", "revenue as of 2019". Returns the closest matches first, with names, argument signatures and one line each, even when none fits, so check them. Next: run_tool, or describe_tool if an argument is unclear.

query.description: What you need, in plain words.

tools.name: describe_tool
tools.description: Read one tool's full description and input JSON Schema, between find_tool and run_tool, when find_tool's signature does not settle an argument. An unknown name returns an error.

name.description: The exact tool name, as find_tool returned it.

tools.name: run_tool
tools.description: Run a tool find_tool named: one ({name, arguments}), or up to 25 ({calls: [...]}). Independent calls run at once; a failed call returns its own error. Read-only unless the paper-trading pack is on. Any argument can be {"$file": "path.csv", "column": "close"} (or "columns": [...] / "all") instead of pasted numbers. {"$result": i, "path": "close"} passes batch call i's output into a later call; every result also has a ref ("r1", ...) later calls pass the same way, {"$result": "r1", "path": "close"}, so data never needs copying.

calls.description: Several calls in one round trip; calls without $result run concurrently.

return.description: Batch: every result (default) or only the last.

digits.description: Round fractional numbers to this many significant figures (default 6; 4 saves tokens); whole numbers never change.

select.description: Only these fields of each result, as dotted paths, e.g. ["verdict", "rows.0.accession"] (rows take column names).

receipt.description: Add input and output SHA-256 and pack versions, to recompute and compare later.

max_chars.description: Cap each result at this many JSON characters; the rest stays under its ref.

as_of.description: As of this past date (YYYY-MM-DD): only what was public then.

changes_only.description: Only what changed since this call last ran in this session.

view.description: Draw the result for the person (charts, statements, yield curves, backtests) where MCP Apps are drawn; you get a summary.

tools.name: history
tools.description: Get a measure (or several, with concepts) over time, newest first: latest (default), first reported, or as known on a filing date, with its filing, other version and yearly change. Use it for one measure across periods or as known on a past date; financial_statements for whole statements. Long answers come in pages.

concept.description: Plain name (revenue, eps_diluted, assets; follows tag changes) or XBRL tag (Revenues).

basis.description: latest (default), first_reported, or as_of (default with as_of).

as_of.description: A filing date, not a period end: only filings made by then count.

unit.description: Default: the unit with most periods.

tools.name: financial_statements
tools.description: A company's financial statements exactly as filed: income statement, balance sheet, cash flow and equity statement from its 10-K (or 10-Q), with its own line labels, each line's XBRL concept and the values as the filing shows them (units say the scale). Joins several filings by period; a line a later filing restated, or that a stock split changed, is shown beside its first-reported figure, never mixed in. Use it for every line in the company's own words; history for one measure over many years.

statement.description: Which statement: income, balance_sheet, cash_flow, comprehensive_income, equity; core (default) is the first three, all is every one.

period.description: annual (10-K, default) or quarterly (10-Q: each quarter and the year to date; the fourth quarter is only in the 10-K's year).

filings.description: How many 10-Ks (or 10-Qs) to read and join by period, newest first; default 1. One 10-K holds three years of income and cash flows and two balance sheets, so 2 covers four years and 3 covers five.

fiscal_year.description: Start from the 10-K for the fiscal year ending in this calendar year (or the latest 10-Q of it).

filed_before.description: Start from the latest filing on or before this date: what was known then.

instructions: Canli Capital's finance tools in one server: 401 tools in 6 packs (quant, validation, fundamentals, research, backtest, markets). history and financial_statements are tools of their own here: call them directly. Common tools, which run_tool takes without a search first (as {name, arguments}) unless listed above: a company's SEC-reported figures over time: history {company, concept} or, for several at once, {company, concepts: [...]} (plain names like revenue or XBRL tags; basis first_reported or latest); figures as known on a date: known_as_of {company, as_of}; statements as filed: financial_statements {company}; filings and their text: list_filings, read_filing, search_filings; prices: price_history {symbol}; macro series: economic_series. For anything else, call the find_tool tool with what you need in plain words; its results include each tool's arguments, so you can usually call run_tool next (describe_tool explains arguments in full). To save tokens: pass long data as {"$file": "path.csv", "column": "close"} instead of pasting numbers; put several calls in one run_tool, using {"$result": i, "path": "field"} to feed one call's output into the next, and return: "last" when only the final answer matters. To show prices (several are compared), markets, yields, statements, options, a backtest, holdings or orders, add view: true: the person gets an interactive view, you a summary. Returns are simple fractions (0.01 = 1%), oldest first. canli://privacy says what each pack sends and stores. To double-check figures in a written draft, verify_claims (through run_tool) marks each confirmed, contradicted (with the filed figure) or not reported; figures that came from these tools need no second check.
